To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

complex-valued neural nets perform on par with real-valued neural nets on classification problems, that complex-valued nets do not require a complex input, but rather learn to handle noise in the input space and that complex-valued activation functions are transferable from the real-valued domain.

1) complex-valued neural nets perform equal to or worse than their real-valued counterparts, 2) complex-valued networks are able to handle noise in the complex plane, 3) the imaginary part of the weights follow the real parts, 4) complex activation functions are easily transferable from the real to complex domain and 5) complex weight initialization remains a problem for complex-valued neural netwroks.
when comparing real- and complex-valued neural nets of similar sizes, the latter performs equal to or slightly below the former on a variety of real-valued datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether complex-valued neural architectures are a viable alternative to real-valued neural networks.
the question whether complex-valued neural models are a viable alternative for real-valued models.
evaluating complex-valued neural models on real-valued classification problems and finding ways to make them more practical.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
complex-valued neural nets are not better, but they can be equal in performance to their real-valued counterparts, and they have some unique capabilities.
complex-valued models are not a panacea for real-valued classification.
the use of complex-valued models does not improve performance over real-valued models on the tasks investigated in this paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
real-valued neural networks should be favoured over complex-valuid neural networks for real-valued tasks.
complex-valued neural nets have a lot of potential but are not yet ready to be used in real-world applications.
complex-valued models do not outperform real-valued models, and that they are not suitable for tasks where the data is real-valued.
The main takeaway from our work is that
complex-valued neural nets do not outperform real-valued neural nets on real-valued classification data, but they do have some unique advantages.
the use of complex-valued models is not justified for the tasks we investigated.
complex-valued neural models are a viable option for real-valued classification problems.
